report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/lanes/graph_brief.py chunk 1 of 2: module docstring, constants, dataclass, symbol/import layers, neighbourhood, and start of graph_brief.
risks: graph_brief | medium | index=None path calls cached_index(root) but chunk ends before handling; uncheckable whether it truly never raises. | Read remainder of graph_brief and its exception handling.

file_symbols | low | Class bases only include ast.Name, so complex bases (e.g., Generic[T]) are omitted; docstring says 'class name' but not full bases. | Check intended contract: does 'class name' imply full base list?

file_symbols | low | Assignments only captured if target is a bare Name and identifier isupper(); constants like `x: int = 1` (AnnAssign) are not captured. | Verify intended scope of 'Top-level API' includes annotated assignments.
_tail_matches | low | Suffix matching may over-match (e.g., `foo.bar` matches `bar.py`), but docstring acknowledges and accepts mislabelling a true edge. | No action needed.

_deep_only_modules | low | Uses `id(node)` and `body = set(map(id, tree.body))`; ast.walk includes nodes from tree.body, so id comparison works, but relies on object identity which is stable during walk. | No action needed.

graph_brief | low | `rels = tuple(dict.fromkeys(...))` deduplicates but does not normalize case or resolve paths; targets may be duplicated in different forms. | Check caller expectations for target normalization.
todos: Read chunk 2 of graph_brief.py to complete review of graph_brief and render_brief.
Verify that cached_index never raises as claimed.
Check whether file_symbols should handle AnnAssign and complex class bases.

handoff.purpose: Review first chunk: module docstring, constants, GraphBrief dataclass, symbol and import layers, neighbourhood, and start of graph_brief.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BUDGET_CHARS
symbols.note: Default budget of 12000 characters, sized from measured symbol layer.

symbols.name: ARTEFACT_ROOTS
symbols.note: Tuple of path prefixes considered artefacts: runs/, build/, dist/, .captures/.

symbols.name: _is_artefact
symbols.note: Returns True if relative path starts with any artefact root.

symbols.name: GraphBrief
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding rendered brief text, targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, and provenance.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.truncated
symbols.note: Property returning True if any dropped layer has items.

symbols.name: _sig
symbols.note: Builds a signature string from an AST function node, including async and *args/**kwargs.

symbols.name: file_symbols
symbols.note: Parses a Python file and returns declaration lines for top-level functions, classes (with methods one level down), and uppercase assignments.

symbols.name: _deep_only_modules
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of dotted module names imported only inside function bodies.

symbols.name: _tail_matches
symbols.note: Checks whether any dotted name in a set plausibly denotes a relative file path via suffix matching.

symbols.name: _neighbourhood
symbols.note: Computes hop-limited neighbourhood of targets using forward and reverse edge maps, excluding artefacts.

symbols.name: graph_brief
symbols.note: Builds a GraphBrief for targets and their neighbourhood; starts by resolving root and deduplicating targets.

claims.text: the agents never see the graph. No provider module references structcore, build_index, typegraph or forest. The entire context a write lane gets is read_inlined_context -- raw file bytes and nothing else.
claims.why: This chunk contains only this module; it cannot observe references in other provider modules or the actual context passed to write lanes.

claims.text: All three of those hallucinations are answered by ~6.5k characters of text that the index can already produce.
claims.why: The claim refers to index capabilities and measured character counts; this chunk does not include the index implementation or measurements.

claims.text: Function-body edges are marked *: 202 of 526 internal edges in this repo are only visible there, so a brief built from top-level imports alone would present ~60% of the graph as the whole of it.
claims.why: The statistics (202/526, 60%) are external measurements not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Layers 2 and 3 degrade cleanly: the type and document layers of the index are behind flags, and when they are off those sections are omitted rather than faked.
claims.why: The implementation of layers 2 and 3 (imports and documents) is not fully present in this chunk; only the import layer's helper functions are shown, and the document layer is not shown at all.

claims.text: What is never omitted silently is a TRUNCATION -- if the budget cuts the brief, the brief says what it dropped.
claims.why: The GraphBrief dataclass has a 'dropped' mapping and a 'truncated' property, but the rendering code that would output the dropped items is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This is a DERIVED artefact. It is regenerated, never edited, and a model must not cite it as evidence about behaviour -- it describes shape, not semantics.
claims.why: This is a policy statement about the artefact's usage; no code in this chunk enforces or contradicts it.

claims.text: Default character budget ... the full symbol layer for the daedalus/ package is 6,479 characters, so a 1-hop brief around a handful of files fits comfortably and the budget only bites on a genuinely wide change.
claims.why: The 6,479 character measurement is external; this chunk only defines the constant.

claims.text: Marks an edge that exists ONLY inside a function body. See the module docstring: this is the 38% of the import graph that naive tooling misses.
claims.why: The percentage 38% is an external statistic; the constant itself is defined.

claims.text: runs/ -- the first brief built for daedalus/shift.py listed runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py as a graph neighbour and printed its symbols. That file is the DESTROYED artefact kept as evidence: a test module that overwrote the real one. Showing it to a model asked to edit shift.py teaches it precisely the substitution the write gate now refuses -- the brief would have been arguing for the bug.
claims.why: The anecdote refers to historical events and other modules; this chunk only shows the artefact root tuple.

claims.text: build/ -- holds 142 stale copies of the package. Every naive sweep double-counts them, and a brief that lists a symbol twice from two versions of one file is worse than one that omits it.
claims.why: The 142 copies is an external measurement; the constant is defined.

claims.text: Characters reserved for the header, which is composed after the layers are budgeted. Generous on purpose: overshooting the reserve wastes a few hundred characters, while under-reserving silently pushes the brief over the budget a caller sized its prompt against.
claims.why: The header composition logic is not in this chunk; only the reserve constant is defined.

claims.text: A rendered brief plus the facts it was rendered from.
claims.why: The dataclass fields (text, targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, provenance) match that description; text is the rendered brief and the others are facts.

claims.text: The files the brief was requested for.
claims.why: The field is named targets and is a tuple of strings; no other meaning is implied.

claims.text: Files pulled in as graph neighbours of the targets.
claims.why: The field is a tuple of strings; the _neighbourhood function returns sorted(seen - set(targets)), which are files beyond targets.

claims.text: Layer name -> number of items rendered.
claims.why: The field is a Mapping[str, int], matching the description.

claims.text: Layer name -> number of items dropped by the budget.
claims.why: The field is a Mapping[str, int], and the truncated property checks any(self.dropped.values()), which is consistent.

claims.text: Signatures rather than bare names, because the measured failure was not only "the module does not exist" but "the module does not define that": a name without its shape still lets a caller invent the arguments.
claims.why: The function uses _sig to produce signatures for functions and methods, and for classes it only outputs the class head plus method signatures, not bare names.

claims.text: Methods are included one level down for classes, since Shift.tick() is the kind of thing a caller needs and the class name alone does not give it.
claims.why: The loop iterates over node.body of the class and includes methods with indentation, one level down.

claims.text: Deeper nesting is deliberately not listed -- it is not API.
claims.why: The loop only inspects node.body of the class, not deeper levels.

claims.text: Never raises for a missing or unreadable index: a lane that cannot get a brief must still be able to run with none. A brief is context, not a gate.
claims.why: The chunk ends right after the call to cached_index(root); exception handling is not visible. The claim cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: index may be supplied to avoid a rebuild; otherwise the process-wide cached index is used, which is single-flight, so two hundred concurrent lanes warm it once rather than each starting a full scan.
claims.why: The single-flight property of cached_index is not visible in this chunk; only the call to cached_index(root) is shown.

claims.text: Computed here rather than read from the index because the index publishes a flat edge list with no depth: it correctly INCLUDES function-body edges (12 edges for offload.py against 7 top-level import statements -- verified), it just cannot say which ones they are.
claims.why: The claim about the index's flat edge list and the 12/7 numbers are external to this chunk; the function itself does compute deep-only modules via an AST pass.

claims.text: One extra AST pass over a handful of neighbour files buys the distinction.
claims.why: The function does an AST parse and walk to identify deep imports.

claims.text: Suffix matching on the dotted path, because a function-body import may be written from .kairos import drafts or import daedalus.kairos.drafts and both denote daedalus/kairos/drafts.py.
claims.why: The function splits the relative path and the dotted names, and compares the last one or two segments, which is suffix matching.

claims.text: Over-matching here only ever adds a * mark to an edge that is genuinely present, so a wrong guess mislabels a true edge rather than inventing one.
claims.why: The function returns True if any dotted name matches the tail; if it over-matches, it only affects the marking of an edge that is already present, not creating a new edge.

observations.what: graph_brief calls cached_index(root) but the chunk ends before showing any exception handling, so the docstring claim 'Never raises for a missing or unreadable index' cannot be verified.

file_symbols only captures class bases that are simple ast.Name nodes; more complex bases (e.g., Generic[T]) are omitted, and the docstring says 'class name' rather than full bases, so this may be acceptable.
file_symbols only captures Assign nodes with a single Name target that is all-uppercase; annotated assignments (AnnAssign) are not captured, which may miss constants like 'X: int = 1'.
_tail_matches uses suffix matching which can over-match (e.g., 'foo.bar' matches 'bar.py'), but the docstring explicitly accepts this as a trade-off.
_deep_only_modules uses id(node) to distinguish top-level vs deep imports, which relies on object identity; since ast.walk yields the same node objects from the tree, this should be correct.
